back: Conditions that balance yield, rate, cost and safety instead of maximising one of them.

front: Four factors when choosing industrial conditions
back: Rate, yield (position of equilibrium), cost and safety.

front: Exothermic reaction: effect of low temperature
back: Higher equilibrium yield, but a slower rate.

front: Effect of high pressure (fewer gas molecules on the right)
back: Higher yield and faster rate, but expensive equipment, more energy and greater risk.

front: Why use a catalyst in industry?
back: Faster rate, so equilibrium is reached quickly at a lower, cheaper temperature; yield unchanged.
So that raw materials are not wasted; almost all are eventually converted.

front: How do exothermic processes save energy?
back: Heat released preheats incoming gases or raises steam for electricity.

front: Why can a lower yield be better?
back: If it is reached much faster, more product is made per hour.
Total cost per day ÷ tonnes of product per day.

front: How does the % ammonia at equilibrium change with conditions?
back: It rises with pressure and falls with temperature.
